text.p: Alluvial tin miner Norminco Ltd said on Friday it had made changes to its board, senior management and its directors would recommend the company restructure its capital at the annual meeting on December 20.

"The proposed changes (details of which will be forwarded to shareholders within the next few weeks) are compatible with a new phase in the company's operations and a new strategic direction," Norminco told the Australian Stock Exchange (ASX).
The company said Garry Allen had been appointed a director and managing director. It said Peter Hampshire would retire from the Board on February 1, 1997.

Norminco also said it had appointed a highly qualified and experienced mining consultant to a permanent role as operations manager and it had accepted the resignations of its mining engineer and project manager.
Norminco said it had kept the ASX informed of its operational difficulties at its Leichhardt Creek tin mine in north Queensland and the tight liquidity problems being experienced by the company.

Last month Norminco announced that it had entered into an agreement with a shareholder for the provision of A$1 million in funds immediately and that the agreement provided for further funding within six months.
"These funds will enable the company to proceed with feasibility studies on the establishment of three new mines," Norminco said.
Norminco is Australia's only sole tin miner.
At 1.40 p.m. (0240 GMT), Norminco shares were traing at 4.9 cents each, up 0.2 cents on the day.
